bibliographic.title: AI chatbots not yet ready for clinical use
bibliographic.authors: Joshua Au Yeung; Zeljko Kraljevic; Akish Luintel; Alfred Balston; Esther Idowu; Richard J. Dobson; James T. Teo
bibliographic.citation_apa: Au Yeung, J., Kraljevic, Z., Luintel, A., Balston, A., Idowu, E., Dobson, R. J., & Teo, J. T. (2023). AI chatbots not yet ready for clinical use. Frontiers in Digital Health, 5, 1161098. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2023.1161098

methodology.study_design: perspective article comparing ChatGPT and Foresight on diagnosis forecasting from clinical vignettes
methodology.sample_description: clinical vignettes used for comparing diagnostic forecasting performance
methodology.technology_context: transformer-based conversational AI and large language models (ChatGPT, GatorTron, Foresight) for healthcare chatbots

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly addresses LLM-based conversational AI in healthcare and discusses clinical limitations and AI safety, but the provided text is a perspective focused on readiness and model comparison rather than explicit conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, audit, compliance, or human oversight frameworks.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and page 1 are available; full-text sections on methods, results, governance considerations, and limitations are needed to confirm eligibility and appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Peer-reviewed perspective with stated comparison of ChatGPT and Foresight on clinical vignettes; appraisal is limited because methods, sample size, results, and detailed safety/governance analysis are not present in the supplied excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The text coherently frames LLM chatbot potential and clinical limitations in healthcare, but the excerpt provides insufficient methodological and governance detail to support high-confidence synthesis on conversational governance.

coding.theme: Readiness and limitations of transformer-based LLM chatbots for clinical use
coding.subtheme: Comparative diagnostic forecasting with general and healthcare-focused LLMs

synthesis.main_claim: LLM-based conversational AI chatbots show growing potential in healthcare, but transformer-based chatbots are not yet ready for clinical use and require important limitations to be considered.
synthesis.contribution: Compares ChatGPT and Foresight on forecasting diagnoses from clinical vignettes and situates emerging transformer/LLM chatbots against prior rules-based or Bayesian healthcare chatbot approaches.
synthesis.limitations: Appraisal is constrained to page 1; the excerpt announces discussion of limitations for clinical use but does not provide full empirical results or governance-operational recommendations.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on clinical readiness, safety concerns, and performance comparison of LLM chatbots in regulated healthcare; not sufficient as central evidence on conversational governance frameworks.

evidence.claim: Article is a peer-reviewed perspective in Frontiers in Digital Health published in 2023.
Study focuses on LLM-based conversational AI/chatbots in healthcare.
evidence.excerpt: As large language models (LLMs) expand and become more advanced, so do the natural language processing capabilities of conversational AI, or "chatbots".

evidence.claim: Specific LLMs named include ChatGPT and healthcare-focused models.
evidence.excerpt: OpenAI's recent release, ChatGPT, uses a transformer-based model to enable human-like text generation and question-answering on general domain knowledge, while a healthcare-specific Large Language Model (LLM) such as GatorTron has focused on the real-world healthcare domain knowledge.

evidence.claim: Authors compare ChatGPT and Foresight on clinical vignette diagnosis forecasting.
evidence.excerpt: we discuss the potential and compare the performance of two different approaches to generative pretrained transformers—ChatGPT, the most widely used general conversational LLM, and Foresight, a GPT (generative pretrained transformer) based model focused on modelling patients and disorders. The comparison is conducted on the task of forecasting relevant diagnoses based on clinical vignettes.

evidence.claim: Article addresses regulated clinical healthcare context.
evidence.excerpt: it is probable that Conversational AI will soon be developed for use in healthcare.

evidence.claim: Clinical limitations and safety are explicit concerns.
evidence.excerpt: We also discuss important considerations and limitations of transformer-based chatbots for clinical use. KEYWORDS large language models, chatbot, natural language processing (computer science), digital health, AI safety, transformer

evidence.claim: Prior healthcare chatbots used non-transformer approaches.
evidence.excerpt: Currently, NLP chatbots in healthcare primarily use rules-based, tree-based or Bayesian algorithms

evidence.claim: No explicit operational governance mechanisms are described in the provided text.
evidence.excerpt: These models have the potential to be used as conversational AI or chatbots in healthcare.
